messages.author: 0b46b709ed258edc
messages.subject: Difference in UDs
parts:
Hi ctmm community,

I am wondering if anyone knows if it is possible to subtract UDs to get the difference in probability distributions? I am trying to understand how space-use changes over time both in terms of short-term shifts (e.g., monthly occurrence distributions), but also long-term range changes (e.g., annual range distributions). I have been using the overlap() function to do this, but this just tells me how similar the UDs are and not necessary where the differences are on the landscape. I have considered subtracting the polygon intersection areas, but I was thinking subtracting the PMF, PDF, or CDF would be a more principled approach. Would this be recommended? Is there a way I could convert the difference into its own UD object for plotting and other downstream analyses?

Thanks for any insight!

All the best,
Odd

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Difference in UDs
parts:
Hi Odd,

Instead of subtracting the UDs, which is not something generally done with PDFs, I would take a look at the distance() function, and specifically method="Bhattacharyya" or method="Mahalanobis", depending on if you want to consider the loss of overlap or the relative (physical) distance apart. This will give you generally acceptable methods for calculating dissimilarity between PDFs that have their uncertainties propagated and are first-order debiased. It's probably worth a short paper if someone has the time to lead it and has a good example dataset.

I would hesitate to apply similarity/dissimilarity measures to occurrence distributions, because those are sensitive to the sampling schedule and data loss. I would instead look at differences between the trajectories/paths, which there are a variety of methods for.

Best,
Chris

messages.subject: Re: Difference in UDs
parts:
Hi Chris,

Appreciate the insight. I had the same reservations about using the occurrence distributions, especially considering my data is quite patchy. Thanks for confirming. 

I have another slightly different question: Do you have any recommendations for obtaining an asymmetric measure of overlap? So instead of asking how similar are the home ranges of animal A and animal B, I want to ask how much of the home range of animal A is shared by animal B? I have done this by dividing the intersection area between 95% UDs of A and B by the total 95% UD area of animal A, but this does not consider the probability distributions. 

Thank again for your help.

Best,
Odd

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Difference in UDs
parts:
Hi Odd,

There's nothing I've seen from the statistics literature that corresponds to an asymmetric, geometric overlap. There are asymmetric divergence measures, like the  Kullback–Leibler divergence, which is behind AIC.

It is possible to construct asymmetric measures analogous to method="encounter" from help('overlap'), but I don't know how that would behave or if it would be easily interpreted, and I still haven't even published method="encounter" yet (which is another open project if anyone is interested).

Best,
Chris
